# Second Largest Digit in a String.

@example The digits are 7, 3, 0 and 7 again, so the set is {0, 3, 7}; without the 7, the biggest left is 3.
"k7b30q7"
=> 3

@example Every digit is a 5, so the set is {5}, and nothing is left once 5 is taken out.
"zz55z5"
=> -1

@example The set is {0, 9}; taking out 9 leaves 0, a real answer and not a missing one.
"x0yy9"
=> 0

# A single letter, and a single digit.
"a"
=> -1

"4"
=> -1

# Every letter and no digit.
"abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz"
=> -1

# Zero is the only digit, twice.
"0m0"
=> -1

# All ten digits, scrambled.
"5h0k3927a6481"
=> 8

# Digits in increasing order: the biggest comes last.
"1c2c5"
=> 2

# The biggest comes first; 5 then beats the 2 for second place, and 4 doesn't.
"9r2r5r4"
=> 5

# The biggest digit comes again after the second one.
"3a9b3c9"
=> 3

# Digits only at the start, in decreasing order.
"641abcdef"
=> 4

# Digits only at the end, far apart.
"uvwxyz91"
=> 1

# 9 appears 128 times: a count kept in a signed char goes negative.
"499999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999999"
=> 4

# 5 appears 256 times: a count kept in an unsigned char wraps to 0.
"955555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555555551"
=> 5

# Random small cases from gen.c (lc check --regen makes them).
@gen 1 small
"79jz681"
=> 8

@gen 2 small
"zbjbj"
=> -1

@gen 3 small
"29067785"
=> 8

@gen 4 small
"77j4"
=> 4

@gen 5 small
"77b777"
=> -1

@gen 6 small
"z2"
=> -1

@gen 7 small
"06z0z4"
=> 4

@gen 8 small
"0000000"
=> -1

# Full-size cases: one digit among letters, and the biggest digit
# repeated with the second one only at the very end.
@gen 3
""
=> -1

@gen 4
""
=> 0
